text: code : Uses J = Sensitivity + Specificity - 1 primary cutoff optimization criterion. Assessment: Youden (1950) commonly used criterion appropriate. However, module lacks cutoff methods clinically important: - Closest (0,1) (minimizes Euclidean distance perfect classifier) - Cost-based optimal cutoff (FN FP costs differ) - Concordance probability method pROC::coords(roc_obj, "best", ...) function supports via best.method argument (options: “youden”, “closest.topleft”). current code uses pROC::coords(roc_obj, "best", ...) non-Youden case (line 881), defaults “youden” anyway — option Youden paths. Recommendation: Expose best.method user option allow “closest.topleft” selection clinical use cases equal weighting sensitivity specificity appropriate. Severity: MODERATE (missing feature, error)

title: Statistical Accuracy Review: enhancedROC.b.R
text: code : Uses pROC::multiclass.roc() implements Hand & Till (2001). : Hand-Till method appropriate multi-class AUC ordinal predictors. However, code also claims calculate OVR (One-vs-Rest) AUC separately (lines 3669-3689), reports Hand-Till result “macro average” average table. incorrect — Hand-Till method pairwise (OVO), macro average OVR AUCs. Reference: Hand DJ, Till RJ (2001). Simple Generalisation Area ROC Curve Multiple Class Classification Problems. Mach Learn, 45:171-186. what: 18. Convex Hull Calculation Uses Full chull() (Lines 1692-1739)
title: Statistical Accuracy Review: enhancedROC.b.R
text: code : Computes full convex hull using grDevices::chull(), filters upper half (diagonal). Assessment: reasonable implementation. ROC convex hull connect (0,0) (1,1) via points maximize performance. Using chull filtering TPR >= FPR correct principle. One concern: code adds (0,0) (1,1) corner points, uses chull(). chull() function returns points outer convex hull counterclockwise order. ROC analysis, want UPPER convex hull. current filtering (hull_tpr_sorted >= hull_fpr_sorted - 1e-10) captures points diagonal, correct upper hull concept. issue full chull() may include lower hull points random classifier line — filtered correctly. Verdict: Correct caveats (implementation works ROC convex hull formally computed using upper convex hull algorithm directly, via full hull + filtering, avoid edge cases).

what: The ClinicoPathJamoviModule: A Comprehensive Open-Source Toolkit for Streamlining Clinicopathological Research
title: Comprehensive Analysis for Clinicopathological Research
text: Background: Clinicopathological research fundamental advancing evidence-based medicine, requires application complex specialized statistical methods. technical barrier programming-based statistical software can limit ability clinicians researchers perform analyses efficiently reproducibly. address gap, developed ClinicoPathJamoviModule, open-source extension user-friendly jamovi statistical platform. Methods: ClinicoPathJamoviModule integrates robust comprehensive suite analytical tools designed address typical workflow clinicopathological data analysis. module built upon R statistical language provides graphical user interface within jamovi wide range functions. Key features include: Descriptive Statistics: Generation publication-ready summary tables (Table 1), advanced stratified analysis (Mantel-Haenszel), mixed model ANOVA repeated measures nested designs. Core Methods: Kaplan-Meier, Nelson-Aalen, Turnbull NPMLE interval-censored data. Advanced Modeling: Cox PH, time-varying effects, AFT models, frailty models. Specialized Applications: Competing risks, multi-state models, recurrent event analysis, cure models. Machine Learning Integration: Survival trees, random forests, gradient boosting, regularized regression (LASSO, Ridge). Oncological Analysis: Specialized methods Progression-Free Survival (PFS), treatment switching (IPCW), tumor growth kinetics. Validation & Reliability: Simulation-based validation power analysis verify analytical results Monte Carlo simulations. Modern Designs: Group sequential, adaptive, platform, master (umbrella, basket) protocols. Epidemiological Tools: Population-based survival analysis, case-cohort designs, attributable risk calculation. Test Evaluation: ROC analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), screening test calculators. Model Validation: Time-dependent ROC, prediction error curves, C-statistics, calibration plots. Sample Size Planning: Precision-based diagnostic test sample size calculation Clopper-Pearson exact CI, automated justification statements, multi-method CI comparison (Wilson, Agresti-Coull, Wald). Inter-rater Statistics: Cohen’s Kappa, Fleiss’ Kappa, Krippendorff’s Alpha, ICC Consensus Scoring: Automated consensus determination majority rule, super-majority, unanimous methods Digital Pathology Validation: Modality comparison glass slides vs digital images HER2-specific analysis Method Comparison: Bland-Altman plots Deming Regression Clinical Monitoring: Alert systems patient monitoring dashboards. Treatment Planning: Optimization frameworks differential diagnosis assistance. Results Interpretation: Laboratory imaging findings correlation. Laboratory Quality Control: Statistical process control, including Shewhart/CUSUM charts, Six Sigma metrics, measurement uncertainty. Spatial Analysis: Spatial point pattern analysis (Ripley’s K-function), spatial autocorrelation (Moran’s ) Texture Analysis: Haralick texture features quantitative pathology Validation Studies: Glass slide vs digital image comparison discordance pattern analysis HER2 Scoring: Specialized tools HER2-low/null distinction ADC therapy eligibility Data Visualization: Advanced plotting tools waterfall plots, swimmer plots, raincloud plots. Data Preprocessing: Utilities data quality checking, missing data management, date corrections. Conclusion: ClinicoPathJamoviModule provides powerful, accessible, free--use toolkit empowers medical researchers conduct sophisticated statistical analyses without requiring extensive programming knowledge. integrating essential functions intuitive jamovi framework, module aims lower barrier high-quality data analysis, enhance research reproducibility, accelerate translation clinical data meaningful insights.

what: Adaptive LASSO for Cox Models — adaptivelasso
title: Adaptive LASSO for Cox Models — adaptivelasso
text: Adaptive LASSO Cox proportional hazards models data-driven penalty selection improved variable selection properties. Unlike standard LASSO, adaptive LASSO uses weights based initial parameter estimates provide consistent variable selection (oracle property) reduced bias non-zero coefficients. implementation supports multiple weight calculation methods, cross-validation optimal penalty selection, stability selection robust variable identification, comprehensive model diagnostics. title: Interrater Reliability — agreement
text: data data data frame. data long format, row unique observation. vars string naming variable data contains diagnosis given observer. baConfidenceLevel Confidence level Bland-Altman limits agreement (LoA). Typically 0.95 95 percent confidence intervals. confLevel Confidence level confidence intervals ICC, CCC, bootstrap CIs, agreement statistics. Default 0.95 (95 percent CI). proportionalBias Test whether difference raters changes systematically magnitude measurement (proportional bias). Uses linear regression difference vs. mean. showBlandAltmanGuide Show educational guide explaining Bland-Altman limits agreement method comparison studies. blandAltmanPlot Generate Bland-Altman plot continuous agreement analysis. Displays mean difference limits agreement first two raters. applicable raters provide continuous measurements (e.g., tumor size mm). agreementHeatmap Generate heatmap visualization agreement patterns categorical data. Creates confusion matrices showing rater pair's classifications correspond. Color-coded cells reveal agreement (diagonal) specific disagreement patterns (-diagonal). Essential identifying systematic biases, problematic categories, training needs. Shows raters agree strongly, consistently disagree, category confusions common. Particularly valuable multi-category classifications complex disagreement patterns. heatmapColorScheme Color palette heatmap visualization. Blue-Red highlights diagonal agreement strong contrast. Traffic light uses intuitive color coding. Viridis perceptually uniform colorblind-safe. Grayscale black--white printing. heatmapShowPercentages Display percentage values within heatmap cells (percentage total cases). Helps interpret relative frequency rater combination. Essential comparing heatmaps different sample sizes. heatmapShowCounts Display absolute counts within heatmap cells (number cases). Shows actual sample sizes cell. Useful identifying cells insufficient data assessing statistical reliability. heatmapAnnotationSize Text size cell annotations (counts percentages). Adjust readability different numbers categories. Larger categories, smaller many categories. showAgreementHeatmapGuide Show educational guide clinical use cases Agreement Heatmap running analysis. sft Display frequency tables showing distribution ratings rater. Useful understanding rating patterns identifying potential biases. wght ordinal variables (e.g., tumor grade G1/G2/G3), weighted kappa accounts degree disagreement. Linear weights: Adjacent disagreements (G1 vs G2) receive partial credit. Squared weights: Larger disagreements (G1 vs G3) penalized heavily. Use 'Unweighted' nominal categories inherent order. exct Use exact p-value calculation instead normal approximation. Recommended small sample sizes (< 30 cases) 3 raters. Note: applicable 2-rater analysis (use Cohen's kappa). showLevelInfo Display information categorical levels currently ordered variables. Essential weighted kappa analysis ensure ordinal levels properly ordered (e.g., G1 → G2 → G3 tumor grades). kripp Alternative reliability measure handles missing data supports various data types. Useful raters rate cases comparing different measurement levels. krippMethod Specifies measurement level Krippendorff's alpha calculation. bootstrap Calculate bootstrap confidence intervals Krippendorff's alpha. showKrippGuide Show educational guide explaining use Krippendorff's Alpha including handling missing data data type selection. gwet Alternative agreement coefficient stable Cohen's kappa dealing high agreement rates unbalanced marginal distributions (e.g., rare tumor subtypes). Gwet's AC corrects paradoxical behavior kappa extreme cases. gwetWeights Unweighted (AC1) nominal categories. Linear Quadratic weights (AC2) ordinal data. showGwetGuide Show educational guide explaining Gwet's AC preferred Cohen's kappa, especially high agreement rates. pabak Prevalence-Adjusted Bias-Adjusted Kappa (PABAK) corrects Cohen's kappa effects prevalence bias. Also reports prevalence index (PI) bias index (BI). Useful kappa paradoxically low despite high agreement (Byrt et al. 1993). Requires exactly 2 raters categorical data. showPABAKGuide Show educational guide explaining PABAK, kappa paradox, prevalence/bias adjustment needed. icc Intraclass Correlation Coefficient continuous measurements (e.g., tumor size mm, biomarker concentrations). Standard measure assessing agreement numeric data. Complements Bland-Altman analysis. showICCGuide Show educational guide explaining use Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, including ICC model selection, interpretation thresholds, clinical examples. iccType ICC model selection. One-way: subject rated different raters. Two-way: subjects rated raters. Random: raters random sample. Mixed: raters fixed. Single: reliability individual rater. Average (k): reliability mean rating. meanPearson Mean Pearson Correlation calculates average linear correlation coefficient across rater pairs continuous measurements. Pearson's r measures linear association variables, ranging -1 (perfect negative) +1 (perfect positive correlation). interrater agreement, high positive correlations indicate raters' measurements vary together linearly. Particularly useful continuous scales (tumor size, biomarker levels, quantitative scores), assumes linear relationship normality. Complements ICC focusing correlation rather absolute agreement. Simple, interpretable measure assessing whether raters rank scale measurements similarly. showMeanPearsonGuide Show educational guide clinical use cases Mean Pearson Correlation running analysis. linCCC Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) measures precision accuracy continuous data, making superior Pearson's r method comparison agreement studies. CCC ranges -1 +1 (perfect concordance) equals product Pearson's r (precision) bias correction factor (accuracy). Unlike Pearson's r measures linear association, CCC penalizes systematic bias. Essential method comparison (manual vs. automated), instrument validation, assessing measurement agreement. Requires 2 raters/methods pairwise comparison; calculates pairwise CCCs 3+ raters. showLinCCCGuide Show educational guide clinical use cases Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient running analysis. tdi Total Deviation Index (TDI) quantifies limits within specified proportion differences two measurement methods fall. Unlike Bland-Altman assumes constant variability, TDI accounts heteroscedastic errors (variance increasing magnitude). title: Brier Score & Integrated Brier Score — brierscore
text: IMPORTANT LIMITATIONS: BASIC implementation single time-point Brier score evaluation. requires PRE-COMPUTED survival probabilities (raw Cox models). Many features listed IMPLEMENTED STATISTICALLY INVALID. Brier Score analysis evaluates calibration accuracy measuring mean squared difference predicted survival probabilities observed outcomes SINGLE specified time point. Lower Brier scores indicate better prediction accuracy (perfect prediction = 0, worst = 1). Includes scaled Brier scores relative null model (Kaplan-Meier curve). SUPPORTED: Multiple time points, Integrated Brier Score (IBS), competing risks, linear predictor inputs, formula inputs, temporal/external validation flags. features may appear UI generate errors used. rigorous clinical validation, use established packages: riskRegression::Score() pec::pec(). implementation validated standards.

text: data data data frame. time Time--event censoring variable. survival analysis, follow-time days, months, years. event Binary event indicator variable (1 = event occurred, 0 = censored). competing risks, can multi-level factor. event_code level event variable represents event interest (e.g., death, progression, recurrence). predicted_survival Pre-computed survival probabilities specified prediction time. 0 1. example, predicted 5-year survival probability Cox model machine learning algorithm. linear_predictor Linear predictor Cox model (log hazard ratio). provided instead predicted_survival, survival probabilities computed using Breslow estimator baseline hazard. prediction_formula Formula prediction model neither predicted_survival linear_predictor provided. Example: "~ age + stage + grade". Cox model fitted internally predictions generated. prediction_time Time point evaluate Brier score (units time variable). example, 60 months 5-year predictions, 1825 days 5-year predictions days. multiple_time_points Calculate Brier scores multiple time points show calibration changes time. time_points Comma-separated list additional time points evaluation. Example: "12, 24, 36, 60" 1, 2, 3, 5 years (months). calculate_ibs Calculate Integrated Brier Score integrating time-dependent Brier score across follow-period. Provides single summary measure overall prediction performance across time. Computationally expensive. ibs_start_time Start time IBS integration. Usually 0 include entire follow-period. ibs_end_time End time IBS integration. exceed maximum follow-time. Determines time horizon prediction performance summarized. scaled_brier Calculate scaled (standardized) Brier score relative null model (Kaplan-Meier survival curve). Scaled Brier = 1 - (Brier_model / Brier_null). Values near 0 indicate improvement KM, positive values indicate better predictions KM. reference_model Compare Brier score reference prediction model assess incremental value new predictors. reference_predictions Pre-computed survival probabilities reference model comparison. reference_formula Formula reference model reference_predictions provided. Example: "~ age + stage" (simpler full model). confidence_intervals Calculate confidence intervals Brier scores using bootstrap influence function methods. Bootstrap method computationally expensive. ci_method Method confidence interval estimation. Bootstrap accurate computationally intensive, influence function faster. bootstrap_samples Number bootstrap samples confidence interval estimation. samples provide stable estimates. confidence_level Confidence level interval estimation. compare_multiple_models Compare Brier scores across multiple prediction models identify best calibrated model. additional_predictions Additional prediction variables (survival probabilities) competing models comparison. model_names Comma-separated names prediction models compared. Used labeling output tables plots. competing_risks Use competing risks framework multiple event types can occur. Brier score accounts cumulative incidence rather survival. cause_specific competing risks, calculate cause-specific Brier score event interest. plot_brier_over_time Plot time-dependent Brier score across follow-period. Shows prediction accuracy changes time. plot_calibration_curve Display calibration curve showing agreement predicted observed survival probabilities. Perfect calibration appears 45° line. calibration_groups Number risk groups calibration curve (e.g., deciles = 10). groups provide finer resolution require larger sample size. plot_model_comparison Bar plot comparing Brier scores across multiple models confidence intervals. plot_integrated_brier Visualize IBS area Brier score curve time. stratified_brier Calculate Brier scores stratified important subgroups assess calibration consistency across populations. stratify_by Variable stratified analysis (e.g., treatment arm, age group, center). inverse_probability_weighting Use inverse probability censoring weighting (IPCW) handle censored observations. Recommended proper Brier score estimation. external_validation Indicate external validation (model developed different dataset). Affects interpretation may trigger additional diagnostics. temporal_validation Indicate temporal validation (recent patients development cohort). May assess calibration drift time. development_period End date development period temporal validation assessment (format: YYYY-MM-DD). missing_handling Method handling missing predictor outcome data. random_seed Random seed bootstrap sampling stochastic procedures.

title: Clinical Hemodynamic Monitoring — clinmon
text: Calculates hemodynamic indices continuous clinical monitoring data. Uses clintools package compute COest, CPPopt, CVRi, Dx, Mx, PI, PRx, PWA, RI, Sx continuous recordings arterial blood pressure, intracranial pressure,  middle cerebral artery blood velocity, heart rate.

title: Clinical Hemodynamic Monitoring — clinmon

title: Clinical Hemodynamic Monitoring — clinmon
text: data data data frame continuous monitoring data. First column must time seconds, followed physiological variables. time_var Time variable seconds. first column contain  continuous time measurements monitoring system. abp Arterial blood pressure measurements mmHg. Used calculating  multiple hemodynamic indices including PRx, Mx, Sx, Dx, CVRi, COest. mcav Middle cerebral artery blood velocity measurements. Used calculating Mx, Sx, Dx, CVRi, PI, RI indices. icp Intracranial pressure measurements mmHg. Used calculating PRx CPPopt indices combined arterial blood pressure. cpp Cerebral perfusion pressure measurements mmHg. Alternative ICP calculating Mx, Sx, Dx indices. hr Heart rate measurements beats per minute. Used calculating estimated cardiac output (COest). freq Frequency recorded data Hz. Default 1000 Hz high-resolution monitoring systems. Adjust based data collection frequency. blocksize Length block seconds. Blocks fundamental units calculating indices. Default 3 seconds. epochsize Size epochs number blocks. Epochs aggregate multiple blocks correlation-based indices. Default 20 blocks. output_level Select output row represent: - Period: Analysis periods (requires trigger data) - Epoch: Epoch-level results (correlation indices available) - Block: Block-level results (correlation indices) - CPPopt: Optimal cerebral perfusion pressure analysis overlapping Enable overlapping calculations correlation-based indices. can improve temporal resolution increases computation time. blockmin Minimum measurements required create block percentage. Blocks less data omitted. Default 50 percent. epochmin Minimum blocks required create epoch percentage. Epochs fewer blocks omitted. Default 50 percent. fast_processing Enable fast processing aggregating data analysis. speeds computation may reduce precision. show_summary Display summary statistics calculated hemodynamic indices. show_detailed Display detailed results table calculated indices time period/epoch/block.

text: data data data frame regression analysis. dep outcome variable regression analysis. Can continuous (linear regression), binary (logistic regression), time--event. covs Independent variables (predictors) include regression model. displayed coefficients plot. model_type Type regression model fit: - Linear: continuous outcomes - Logistic: binary outcomes (odds ratios) - Cox: survival analysis (hazard ratios) - Poisson: count outcomes (rate ratios) time_var Time--event variable Cox regression. required  model type set Cox regression. include_intercept Include intercept term coefficient plot. Usually  excluded often primary interest. coef_selection select coefficients display plot. specific_coefs Comma-separated list coefficient names include exclude  (depending selection method). Leave blank use coefficients. ci_level Confidence level coefficient confidence intervals (e.g., 0.95 95 percent CI). inner_ci_level Optional inner confidence interval enhanced visualization. Set 0 disable inner CI. Common values 0.8 0.9. sort_coefs order coefficients plot. Magnitude sorting can help identify important predictors. decreasing_sort sorting magnitude alphabetically, use decreasing order. horizontal_plot Display coefficients horizontally (default) vertically. Horizontal layout typically preferred readability. point_size Size coefficient points plot. line_thickness Thickness confidence interval lines. standardize Standardize coefficients scaling predictors mean 0 SD 1. Useful comparing effect sizes across variables different scales. robust_se Use robust (sandwich) standard errors confidence intervals. Recommended concerns heteroscedasticity. exp_transform Exponentiate coefficients show odds ratios (logistic), hazard ratios (Cox), rate ratios (Poisson). Automatically enabled logistic Cox models. compare_models Create comparison plots multiple model specifications. Useful sensitivity analysis model selection. model2_covs Covariates second model comparison. used comparing models. model3_covs Covariates third model comparison. used comparing models. model_names Comma-separated names models comparing multiple models. used legend. show_coefficient_plot Display main coefficient plot confidence intervals. show_model_summary Display statistical summary fitted model(s) including R-squared, AIC, fit statistics. show_coefficient_table Display detailed table coefficients, standard errors, p-values. custom_title Custom title coefficient plot. Leave blank automatic title. custom_x_label Custom label x-axis. Leave blank automatic label based model type.

Usually higher control group effective treatments. survival_distribution Assumed underlying survival distribution. title: Concordance Index (Harrell's C-index) — concordanceindex
text: Harrell's concordance index (C-index) evaluating discrimination ability survival prediction models. C-index measures proportion comparable pairs patients model correctly ranks survival times - generalization ROC curve's AUC censored survival data. Values range 0.5 (discrimination) 1.0 (perfect discrimination), 0.7-0.8 considered good >0.8 considered excellent. Unlike time-dependent ROC evaluates specific time points, C-index provides global measure across entire follow-period. Supports time-dependent concordance dynamic predictions, competing risks extensions, stratified analysis, comparison models. Essential validating Cox regression models, machine learning survival predictions, prognostic scores. C-index accounts censoring appropriate pair weighting can decomposed identify risk groups contribute discrimination.

Can include numeric,  ordinal, nominal variables. algorithm handles mixed-type predictors optimally. strata Optional stratification variable stratified survival analysis. Creates separate baseline hazards stratum. teststat Test statistic use. 'quad' uses quadratic form multivariate tests, 'max' uses maximum-type statistic. Quadratic form powerful small effects, maximum-type large effects. testtype Multiple testing correction method. Bonferroni provides conservative reliable correction. Monte Carlo uses permutation-based p-values. mincriterion Minimum criterion (1 - p-value) variable selection. Higher values create conservative trees fewer splits. Default 0.95 corresponds significance level 0.05. minsplit Minimum number observations required node splitting. Higher values create simpler trees reduce overfitting. minbucket Minimum number observations terminal nodes. smaller minsplit. Higher values increase tree stability. maxdepth Maximum depth tree. Deeper trees may overfit, shallower trees may underfit. nresample Number Monte Carlo resamples p-value computation using Monte Carlo test type. resamples provide accurate p-values increase computation time. logrank_scores Use log-rank scores survival splitting. TRUE, uses log-rank statistics optimized survival data. Leave empty use variables. Setting creates random forest-like approach. replace Use bootstrap sampling replacement tree construction. title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis — costeffectiveness
text: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA) evaluating economic value diagnostic tests, screening programs, clinical decision strategies. Calculates Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER), represents additional cost per additional unit effectiveness (e.g., cost per correct diagnosis, cost per QALY gained). analysis compares new diagnostic strategies standard care alternative approaches, visualizing results cost-effectiveness plane calculating net monetary benefit various willingness--pay thresholds. Essential health technology assessment, budget impact analysis, justifying adoption new diagnostic technologies multiplex IHC, AI-assisted pathology, digital pathology platforms, molecular tests. Supports deterministic sensitivity analysis (tornado plots) identify key cost drivers probabilistic sensitivity analysis (Monte Carlo simulation) quantify uncertainty cost-effectiveness conclusions. Particularly valuable demonstrating value proposition advanced diagnostics hospital administrators, payers, policy makers.

title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis — costeffectiveness
code: costeffectiveness(   data,   strategy,   comparator_level,   cost,   effectiveness,   effectiveness_type = "binary",   effectiveness_label = "Correct Diagnoses",   calculate_icer = TRUE,   calculate_incremental = TRUE,   dominance_analysis = FALSE,   net_monetary_benefit = FALSE,   wtp_threshold = 50000,   multiple_wtp_thresholds = FALSE,   wtp_range = "0, 25000, 50000, 100000, 150000",   confidence_intervals = FALSE,   ci_method = "bootstrap",   bootstrap_samples = 1000,   confidence_level = 0.95,   deterministic_sensitivity = FALSE,   sensitivity_parameters =     "test_cost, follow_up_cost, test_sensitivity, test_specificity",   sensitivity_range_pct = 20,   probabilistic_sensitivity = FALSE,   psa_simulations = 1000,   cost_distribution = "gamma",   effect_distribution = "normal",   voi_analysis = FALSE,   evpi_population = 10000,   evppi_parameters = FALSE,   evppi_focus = "both",   subgroup_analysis = FALSE,   subgroup_variable,   time_horizon = 1,   discount_costs = FALSE,   discount_rate_costs = 3,   discount_effects = FALSE,   discount_rate_effects = 3,   plot_ce_plane = TRUE,   plot_ce_acceptability = FALSE,   plot_nmb = FALSE,   plot_tornado = FALSE,   plot_incremental_frontier = FALSE,   perspective = "healthcare",   include_indirect_costs = FALSE,   currency = "USD",   cost_year = 2024,   handling_missing = "complete",   random_seed = 12345 )

title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis — costeffectiveness
text: data data data frame. strategy Variable indicating diagnostic strategy used observation. least 2 levels (e.g., "New Test" vs. "Standard Care"). comparator_level level strategy variable represents comparator (baseline/reference) strategy others compared. cost Total cost per patient diagnostic strategy. include relevant costs: test costs, follow-procedures, treatment costs, adverse events. Express consistent currency units (e.g., USD, EUR). effectiveness Effectiveness measure per patient. Can correct diagnoses (0/1), QALYs, life-years gained, cancers detected, etc. Higher values represent better outcomes. effectiveness_type Type effectiveness measure analyzed. Affects interpretation labeling ICER results. effectiveness_label Custom label effectiveness measure (e.g., "Cancers Detected", "True Positives", "QALYs"). calculate_icer Calculate Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio. ICER = (Cost_new - Cost_comparator) / (Effect_new - Effect_comparator). Represents additional cost per additional unit effectiveness. calculate_incremental Display incremental costs effects relative comparator strategy. dominance_analysis Identify dominated strategies (costly less effective) extended dominance (strategies inefficient frontier). net_monetary_benefit Calculate Net Monetary Benefit (NMB) specified willingness--pay thresholds. NMB = (Effectiveness × WTP) - Cost. Positive NMB indicates cost-effective threshold. wtp_threshold Willingness--pay threshold primary analysis (e.g., $50,000 per QALY US, £20,000-30,000 per QALY UK). Used net benefit calculation. multiple_wtp_thresholds Evaluate cost-effectiveness multiple willingness--pay thresholds show robustness conclusions. wtp_range Comma-separated list willingness--pay thresholds analysis. Example: "0, 20000, 30000, 50000, 100000". confidence_intervals Calculate confidence intervals mean costs, mean effects, ICER using bootstrap parametric methods. ci_method Method confidence interval estimation. Bootstrap recommended cost data (often skewed). BCa (Bias-Corrected Accelerated) provides better coverage skewed distributions. bootstrap_samples Number bootstrap resamples confidence interval estimation. confidence_level Confidence level interval estimation. deterministic_sensitivity One-way sensitivity analysis varying individual parameters assess impact ICER. Creates tornado diagram showing influential parameters. sensitivity_parameters Comma-separated list parameter names deterministic sensitivity analysis. column names data. sensitivity_range_pct Percentage variation around base case sensitivity analysis. example, 20 percent means vary parameters 80 percent 120 percent base value. probabilistic_sensitivity Monte Carlo simulation propagate uncertainty parameters simultaneously. Generates cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC) showing probability cost-effectiveness different WTP thresholds. psa_simulations Number Monte Carlo simulations probabilistic sensitivity analysis. cost_distribution Probability distribution cost parameter uncertainty. Gamma recommended costs (non-negative, often right-skewed). effect_distribution Probability distribution effectiveness parameter uncertainty. Beta recommended proportions, normal continuous measures. voi_analysis Calculate Expected Value Perfect Information (EVPI) quantify expected cost uncertainty decision. EVPI represents maximum value conducting research eliminate parameter uncertainty. evpi_population Population size affected decision relevant time horizon. EVPI calculated per-person multiplied population give total value eliminating uncertainty. evppi_parameters Calculate Expected Value Perfect Parameter Information (EVPPI) specific parameters. Shows parameters contribute decision uncertainty. evppi_focus parameters include EVPPI calculation. Useful identifying whether cost effectiveness uncertainty drives decision uncertainty. subgroup_analysis Perform cost-effectiveness analysis stratified subgroups identify populations new strategy cost-effective. subgroup_variable Variable defining subgroups stratified analysis (e.g., disease stage, age group, risk category). time_horizon Time horizon cost-effectiveness analysis years. Short-term diagnostic tests (1 year), longer treatments affecting survival. discount_costs Apply discounting future costs (relevant multi-year time horizons). discount_rate_costs Annual discount rate future costs (typically 3-5 percent health economics). discount_effects Apply discounting future health effects (QALYs, life-years). discount_rate_effects Annual discount rate future effects (often cost discount rate). plot_ce_plane Scatter plot showing incremental costs (y-axis) vs. incremental effects (x-axis). Quadrants indicate dominance relationships. Willingness--pay threshold shown diagonal line. plot_ce_acceptability CEAC showing probability strategy cost-effective across range willingness--pay thresholds. Requires probabilistic sensitivity analysis. plot_nmb Bar plot showing net monetary benefit strategy specified WTP threshold. Strategy highest NMB optimal. plot_tornado Tornado diagram showing one-way sensitivity analysis results. Parameters ordered impact ICER, showing range ICER values across parameter uncertainty ranges. plot_incremental_frontier Plot showing efficient frontier connecting non-dominated strategies. perspective Perspective cost-effectiveness analysis determines costs included. Healthcare system includes direct medical costs, societal includes productivity losses patient time costs. include_indirect_costs Include indirect costs (productivity losses, patient time) societal perspective. currency Currency cost reporting (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY). cost_year Reference year cost values (inflation adjustment needed). handling_missing Method handling missing cost effectiveness data. random_seed Random seed bootstrap Monte Carlo simulations.

title: EM-Algorithm Frailty Models — emfrailty
text: data data data frame elapsedtime Survival time follow-duration variable. contain positive  numeric values representing time event censoring. outcome Event indicator variable specifying whether event interest occurred. Can coded 0/1, TRUE/FALSE, factor levels. covariates Predictor variables frailty model. Can include continuous variables, factors, interactions. included fixed effects model. frailty_variable Variable defining frailty groups (clusters). unique value represents different frailty group sharing common unobserved risk factors. outcomeLevel Specifies level outcome variable represents event interest. numeric variables, typically '1'. factors, specify appropriate level name. frailty_distribution Distribution assumed frailty terms. Gamma commonly used provides conjugate properties efficient EM estimation. estimation_method Method parameter estimation. Standard EM robust, accelerated variants may converge faster large datasets. baseline_hazard Specification baseline hazard function. Parametric forms provide efficiency non-parametric allows maximum flexibility. ties_method Method handling tied event times. Breslow fastest, Efron accurate, exact method precise computationally intensive. confidence_level Confidence level parameter confidence intervals hypothesis tests. max_iterations Maximum number EM algorithm iterations forced termination. convergence_tolerance Convergence tolerance EM algorithm. title: Extremely Randomized Trees for Survival — extratrees
text: Extremely Randomized Trees (Extra Trees) survival analysis using ranger package implementation. method extends random forests introducing additional randomization variable selection split point selection, leading increased bias reduced variance computational efficiency. algorithm particularly effective high-dimensional survival data, large datasets, scenarios requiring fast training prediction. Features include built-variable importance measures, --bag error estimation, support competing risks, excellent scalability. Ideal exploratory analysis, baseline modeling, ensemble methods survival prediction tasks.

text: data data data frame. time Time event variable (numeric). right-censored data,  time study entry event censoring. event Event indicator variable. survival analysis: 0 = censored, 1 = event. competing risks: 0 = censored, 1+ = different event types. predictors Variables use tree construction. Can include numeric, ordinal, nominal variables. algorithm handles mixed-type predictors efficiently. strata Optional stratification variable stratified survival analysis. Creates separate baseline hazards stratum. num_trees Number trees forest. trees generally improve stability performance increase computation time. 500-2000 typical. mtry Number variables randomly selected split. Square root total variables default. Smaller values increase randomization. mtry_custom Custom number variables per split mtry set 'custom'. 1 total number predictors. min_node_size Minimum number observations terminal nodes. Larger values create simpler trees reduce overfitting, smaller values allow complex patterns. max_depth Maximum depth trees. 0 means limit. Deep trees may overfit, shallow trees may underfit. Usually left unlimited Extra Trees. splitrule Splitting criterion. 'extratrees' uses extreme randomization, 'logrank' uses log-rank statistic, 'C' optimizes concordance index, 'maxstat' uses maximally selected rank statistics. num_random_splits Number random splits try per variable Extra Trees rule. Higher values reduce randomization may improve performance. sample_fraction Fraction observations sampled tree. Values < 1.0 create subsampled forests can improve generalization reduce computation. replace Use bootstrap sampling (replacement) tree. FALSE, uses subsampling without replacement. case_weights Optional variable containing case weights observations. Higher weights give observations influence tree construction. importance Method calculating variable importance. Permutation importance measures prediction accuracy decrease variables permuted. Impurity importance measures decrease node impurity. scale_permutation Scale permutation importance standard error. Provides stable importance measures especially correlated predictors. keep_inbag Store observations -bag tree. Required post-processing analyses increases memory usage. oob_error Calculate --bag prediction error. Provides unbiased estimate model performance without need separate validation set. probability Estimate survival probabilities instead hazard ratios. Useful risk prediction probability-based decisions. show_forest_summary Display summary statistics Extra Trees forest including OOB error, variable importance rankings, model parameters. show_importance Display detailed variable importance measures rankings statistical significance tests. show_oob_predictions Display --bag predictions model evaluation risk stratification analysis. plot_importance Create variable importance plot showing relative importance predictors confidence intervals. plot_oob_error Plot --bag error function number trees assess convergence optimal forest size. plot_survival Create Kaplan-Meier survival curves risk groups defined Extra Trees predictions statistical comparisons. plot_partial Generate partial dependence plots top variables showing marginal effects survival predictions. regularization Regularization parameter Extra Trees. Values > 1 increase randomization, values < 1 reduce . 1.0 standard Extra Trees. alpha Significance level variable importance testing confidence intervals plots. num_threads Number threads parallel computation. 0 uses available cores. Parallel computation significantly speeds training. random_seed Random seed reproducible results. Change get different random forests bootstrap samples.

title: Firth's Penalized Likelihood Regression — firthregression
text: Firth's penalized likelihood regression logistic (binary outcome) Cox proportional hazards (survival) models. Addresses small-sample bias, complete/quasi-complete separation, rare events adding Jeffreys-prior penalty likelihood. Provides profile likelihood confidence intervals, penalized likelihood ratio tests, separation diagnostics. Particularly valuable clinical settings low event counts, unbalanced predictors, standard maximum likelihood estimates become infinite due separation.

title: Firth's Penalized Likelihood Regression — firthregression

title: Firth's Penalized Likelihood Regression — firthregression
text: data data data frame. analysisType Type regression model. Logistic uses logistf package binary outcomes Jeffreys-prior bias reduction. Cox uses coxphf package survival outcomes Firth-type penalized partial likelihood. time Time event variable (numeric). Required Cox regression. right-censored data, time study entry event censoring. outcome Outcome variable. logistic regression, binary variable. Cox regression, event indicator (0 = censored, 1 = event). outcomeLevel Level outcome variable treated event interest. predictors Variables include model. Can include continuous, ordinal, nominal variables. suitabilityCheck Assess data suitable selected Firth regression model. ciLevel Confidence level confidence intervals. Default 0.95 95 percent confidence intervals. ciMethod Method computing confidence intervals. Profile likelihood CIs recommended accurate, especially small samples near separation. Wald CIs faster can unreliable situations. separationCheck Check complete quasi-complete separation data. Separation causes standard maximum likelihood fail infinite coefficient estimates. compareStandard Fit standard (unpenalized) model alongside Firth's penalized model show bias reduction. Useful assessing much penalty changes estimates. showModelFit Display model fit statistics including log-likelihood AIC. forestPlot Forest plot showing odds ratios (logistic) hazard ratios (Cox) confidence intervals log scale. separationPlot Diagnostic visualization showing data distributions outcome predictor. title: Generalized Estimating Equations — geemodel
text: data data data frame outcome outcome variable (dependent variable); can continuous, binary, count predictors predictor variables (independent variables) model cluster_id variable identifying clusters (e.g., patient ID, dog ID). Observations ID treated correlated. time_var longitudinal data, specifies time ordering within clusters. Used AR(1) correlation structure. family distribution family link function outcome variable. Gaussian continuous, Binomial binary, Poisson counts. corstr Working correlation structure within clusters: - Exchangeable: constant correlation pairs (recommended starting point) - AR(1): correlation decays time lag (longitudinal data) - Unstructured: estimates pairwise correlations (requires many observations) - Independence: correlation (equivalent GLM) robust_se sandwich estimator standard errors (recommended). Provides valid inference even correlation structure misspecified. conf_level confidence level confidence intervals (default 95 percent) qic Quasi-likelihood Independence Model Criterion. Lower QIC indicates better model fit. Use comparing models. posthoc compare levels categorical predictors using estimated marginal means posthoc_adjust multiple testing correction post-hoc comparisons diagnostics display model diagnostics including number clusters, observations per cluster correlation_plot visualize estimated within-cluster correlation structure

title: Grey-zone (Fuzzy) ROC Analysis — greyzoneroc
text: Grey-zone ROC analysis diagnostic tests uncertainty around decision thresholds requires "know" "defer decision" option. Unlike traditional binary ROC forces every case positive negative, grey-zone ROC acknowledges diagnostic uncertainty creating indeterminate zone around threshold additional testing expert review recommended. Essential AI model deployment uncertain predictions drive clinical decisions, cytology atypical findings requiring repeat sampling, biomarker cutoffs borderline values need confirmation. analysis determines optimal grey-zone boundaries maximize diagnostic certainty minimizing inconclusive results, calculates performance metrics excluding vs including grey-zone cases, provides clinical decision rules handling uncertain classifications. text: Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI) analysis assessing incremental value new biomarkers risk factors prediction models. IDI quantifies improvement model discrimination measuring difference predicted probabilities events non-events new model compared baseline model. Unlike NRI focuses reclassification, IDI provides numeric measure discrimination improvement without requiring risk categories. analysis includes confidence intervals bootstrap methods, statistical significance testing, decomposition event non-event components. Essential biomarker validation, model enhancement assessment, demonstrating clinical utility new predictors medical research. text: data data data frame. source Starting entity relationship. Select variable containing "" nodes. Clinical Examples: • Gene regulatory networks: Regulator gene (e.g., TP53, BRCA1) • Patient networks: First patient similarity pair (Patient_ID) • Disease co-occurrence: Primary diagnosis (ICD10 code) • Protein interactions: Upstream protein • Treatment pathways: Initial intervention target Ending entity relationship. Select variable containing "" nodes. Clinical Examples: • Gene regulatory networks: Target gene regulated (e.g., CDK4, MYC) • Patient networks: Second patient similarity pair • Disease co-occurrence: Secondary diagnosis comorbidity • Protein interactions: Downstream protein • Treatment pathways: Next intervention sequence weight Optional numeric measure connection strength importance. Clinical Examples: • Gene networks: Correlation coefficient (0-1), fold-change, interaction score • Patient networks: Similarity score (e.g., Jaccard index, cosine similarity) • Disease co-occurrence: Number co-occurrences relative risk • Protein interactions: Binding affinity (Kd) confidence score • Treatment pathways: Transition probability (0-1) Leave empty unweighted networks (edges treated equally). group Optional grouping variable color-coding entities. Examples: Gene families,  patient subtypes, disease categories, functional classifications. analysisPreset Choose preset configuration optimized specific clinical research scenarios.  Gene networks focus regulatory relationships, patient networks similarity patterns,  pathway networks biological processes, comorbidity networks disease associations. showNodes Whether display node points along arc baseline. enabled, nodes shown circles sorted positions. nodeSize Method determining node sizes. 'Fixed' uses constant size, 'Degree' scales nodes proportionally connectivity (number connections). nodeSizeValue Size nodes using fixed sizing, base size multiplier using degree-based sizing. Range: 0.1 10. sortNodes Order nodes arranged along baseline. 'None' preserves original order, 'Name' sorts alphabetically, 'Group' clusters categories, 'Degree' orders connectivity. sortDecreasing sorting nodes, whether use descending order. applies Sort Nodes 'None'. horizontal Layout orientation arc diagram. TRUE, nodes arranged horizontally arcs . FALSE, nodes arranged vertically arcs side. arcWidth Method determining arc line widths. 'Fixed' uses constant width, 'Weight' scales arc thickness proportionally edge weights. arcWidthValue Width arcs using fixed sizing, base width using weight-based sizing. Range: 0.1 5. arcTransparency Transparency level arc lines. 0 = fully transparent (invisible), 1 = fully opaque. Lower values reduce visual clutter dense networks. directed Whether treat network directed (edges direction source target) undirected (edges represent bidirectional relationships). aggregateEdges "RECOMMENDED: Combine multiple edges nodes summing weights. matters: Ensures network density <= 1.0 (without aggregation, density can exceed 1.0) Prevents inflated centrality measures Provides accurate statistical summaries Example: Gene →Gene B appears 3 times weights (2, 3, 5), aggregation creates single edge weight 10. disable: specifically need preserve parallel edges specialized analyses." weightMode "edge weights interpreted centrality calculations. STRENGTH mode (default): Higher values = stronger connections Use : Correlations, interaction scores, similarity indices   Examples: r=0.8 (strong), binding affinity score=90 DISTANCE mode: Higher values = longer paths/weaker connections   Use : Costs, physical distances, dissimilarity measures   Examples: Euclidean distance, cost metrics clinical/biological networks use STRENGTH mode." arcColorMode color arcs nodes grouped. 'Source' colors arcs source node's group, 'Target' target node's group, 'Gradient' creates gradient source target colors. applies Color Nodes Group enabled. colorByGroup grouping variable specified, whether color-code nodes group membership. Requires group variable. showStats Whether display network statistics including number nodes, edges, density, centrality measures. showLegend Whether display color legend nodes colored groups. appears grouping variable specified color group enabled. labelSize Size node labels (text). 0.8 standard size, values 1.0 increase label size, 1.0 decrease . Range: 0.1 2.0. plotTitle Optional title display arc diagram. Leave empty title. showSummary Whether display natural-language summary paragraph suitable copying reports publications. Includes network overview, key findings, grouping information. showAssumptions Whether display detailed assumptions, interpretation guidelines, common pitfalls panel. Includes network requirements, centrality measure explanations, important notes proper interpretation. showGlossary Whether display glossary panel definitions key network analysis terms (nodes, edges, centrality measures, density). title: Dot Chart — jjdotplotstats
text: data data data frame. dep continuous numeric variable distribution displayed across different groups using dot plots. group categorical variable defines groups comparison. level displayed separate group dot plot. grvar Optional grouping variable create separate dot plots level variable (grouped analysis). typestatistics Choose appropriate statistical test: Parametric (t-test) assumes normal distribution equal variances; Nonparametric (Mann-Whitney U) makes distribution assumptions; Robust uses trimmed means handle outliers; Bayesian provides evidence strength via Bayes factors. effsizetype Effect size quantifies practical significance: Cohen's d shows standardized difference groups (small=0.2, medium=0.5, large=0.8); Hedge's g corrects small samples; Eta/Omega-squared show proportion variance explained (small=0.01, medium=0.06, large=0.14). centralityplotting Display lines showing central tendency (mean, median, trimmed mean) group. Helps visualize group differences glance. centralitytype Type central tendency display: Mean average sensitive outliers; Median middle value robust outliers; Trimmed mean excludes extreme values; Bayesian provides probabilistic estimate. mytitle Main title plot. Leave blank automatic title generation based variables. xtitle Label horizontal axis showing continuous variable values. Leave blank use variable name. ytitle Label vertical axis showing group categories. Leave blank use variable name. originaltheme Use original ggstatsplot theme instead jamovi's default theme. original theme may suitable publications. resultssubtitle Display statistical test results (p-value, effect size, confidence interval) subtitle plot. Recommended analyses. testvalue Reference value hypothesis testing (usually 0 group comparisons). Can changed test specific clinically meaningful value. bfmessage Display Bayes Factor interpretation (evidence strength) using Bayesian analysis. BF > 3 indicates moderate evidence, BF > 10 strong evidence. conflevel Confidence level intervals (0.95 = 95 percent confidence interval). represents probability true population parameter lies within calculated interval. 95 percent standard analyses. k Number decimal places statistical results (p-values, effect sizes). decimal places show greater precision may clinically meaningful. testvalueline Display vertical reference line test value. Useful showing clinically significant thresholds normal reference ranges. centralityparameter central tendency measure show vertical line plot. Mean sensitive outliers; median robust skewed data. centralityk Decimal places central tendency values displayed plot. match precision meaningful measurement scale. plotwidth Width plot pixels. Larger values provide detail may fit well reports. Default: 650 pixels. plotheight Height plot pixels. Adjust based number groups ensure readability. Default: 450 pixels.

title: Histogram — jjhistostats
text: data data data frame. dep One continuous numeric variables histograms created. Multiple variables displayed separate panels. grvar Optional grouping variable create separate histograms level variable (grouped analysis). typestatistics Type statistical test normality assessment. 'parametric' uses Shapiro-Wilk test, 'nonparametric' uses Anderson-Darling test, 'robust' uses robust normality tests, 'bayes' provides Bayesian analysis. centralityline Whether display vertical line indicating measure central tendency (mean parametric, median nonparametric). changebinwidth Whether manually specify bin width. Smaller values create bins, larger values create fewer bins. resultssubtitle Whether display statistical test results subtitle plot, including normality test results descriptive statistics. showInterpretation Generate clinical interpretation histogram results including distribution shape, normality assessment, practical implications clinical data. Note: Testing 0 rarely clinically meaningful biomedical data. title: Pie Charts — jjpiestats
text: data data data frame. dep categorical variable display pie chart. variable used create pie slices representing proportion category. Must factor variable. group Optional grouping variable creating contingency table analysis. specified, creates 2x2 2xN contingency table performs association tests (Chi-square, Fisher's exact test, etc.). grvar Optional variable create separate pie charts level grouping variable. Creates panel pie charts, one group level (e.g., separate charts treatment center study site). typestatistics Type statistical test categorical association analysis. 'parametric' uses Pearson's Chi-square test, 'nonparametric' uses contingency table tests, 'robust' uses robust association measures, 'bayes' provides Bayesian analysis Bayes factors. originaltheme Whether apply original ggstatsplot theme layer plot. TRUE, uses ggstatsplot's default styling. FALSE, uses jamovi's default ggplot2 theme consistency analyses. counts variable data containing counts, NULL row represents single observation. Use data  already aggregated/tabulated. ratio comma-separated list expected proportions proportion test  (sum 1). example: '0.5,0.5' two equal groups  '0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25' four equal groups. Leave empty equal  theoretical proportions. paired Logical indicating whether data came within-subjects repeated measures design study (Default: FALSE). TRUE, McNemar's test used. FALSE, Pearson's chi-square test used. label information needs displayed label  pie slice. digits Number digits decimal point statistical results. conflevel Confidence/credible interval level. proportiontest Decides whether proportion test x variable carried level y. bfmessage Display Bayes Factor favor null hypothesis. relevant parametric test. messages Display statistical messages console.  Disabling improves performance. clinicalpreset Predefined configurations common clinical scenarios.  Automatically sets appropriate statistical methods parameters. showexplanations Display detailed explanations statistical methods, assumptions, clinical interpretations guide analysis result interpretation. resultssubtitle Whether display statistical test results subtitle pie chart. Shows test statistics, p-values, effect sizes, confidence intervals categorical association tests. Provides detailed statistical summary. showSummary Display natural-language summary paragraph key findings suitable copying reports publications. showAssumptions Display statistical assumptions panel detected violations, warnings chi-square expected counts, Fisher exact test recommendations. showInterpretation Display effect size interpretation guidelines (Cramér's V thresholds), clinical context based analysis preset, methodological notes. addGGPubrDonut Add modern donut chart variant using ggpubr. ggpubrDonutPalette Color palette donut chart.

title: River Plots — jjriverplot
text: 'Function generating river plots (alluvial diagrams) visualize flows transitions time categories.'

title: River Plots — jjriverplot
code: jjriverplot(   data,   id = NULL,   time,   strata,   weight = NULL,   plotType = "alluvial",   fillType = "first",   sortStreams = TRUE,   labelNodes = TRUE,   curveType = "cardinal",   showCounts = FALSE,   showLegend = TRUE,   mytitle = "",   xtitle = "",   ytitle = "",   originaltheme = FALSE )

title: River Plots — jjriverplot
text: data data data frame. id Optional identifier individual entities (e.g., patient ID, customer ID). Useful tracking individual pathways flow diagram. required aggregated flow visualization. time Variable representing time points sequential stages flow. Required longitudinal river plots. Use ordered factors proper time sequence (e.g., 'Baseline', 'Month_3', 'Month_6'). Leave empty using wide format data multiple strata variables. strata Variables containing categories flow stages. longitudinal data: single variable categories (e.g., treatment_response). wide format: multiple variables representing stages (e.g., baseline, month3, month6). variable factor meaningful category names. weight Optional numerical variable determine stream width proportional values. Examples: cost, patient count, revenue, frequency. provided, stream widths represent equal counts/frequencies. Use emphasizing quantitative importance different flows. plotType Type flow visualization. 'alluvial' creates flowing streams stages curved connections, ideal tracking transitions. 'sankey' creates directed flow diagrams straighter connections, good process flows. 'stream' creates stacked area plots time, suitable showing composition changes. fillType Determines colors assigned flow streams. 'first' colors flows based initial category (useful tracking origins). 'last' colors final category (useful tracking destinations). 'frequency' uses flow volume determine colors (emphasizes major flows). sortStreams Whether sort alluvial streams frequency/size. TRUE, larger flows positioned prominently, making major pathways easier identify. Recommended analyses highlight dominant patterns data. labelNodes Whether display category labels nodes (vertical bars). Labels help identify segment represents. Recommended plots unless space limited labels overlap. curveType Shape connecting curves stages. 'cardinal' creates smooth flowing curves (aesthetic). 'linear' creates straight connections (clearest flow direction). 'basis' creates smooth curves. 'step' creates stepped connections (good discrete processes). showCounts Whether display numerical counts values nodes. Shows exact frequencies sums category stage. Useful precise quantitative interpretation may clutter visualization many categories present. showLegend Whether display color legend explaining category mappings. Recommended colors represent meaningful categories. Can hidden save space category labels clearly visible diagram . mytitle Main title river plot. describe flow visualized (e.g., 'Patient Treatment Pathways Time', 'Customer Journey Analysis'). Leave empty title. xtitle Label x-axis, typically describing time dimension stages (e.g., 'Study Timepoint', 'Process Stage', 'Academic Year'). Leave empty use variable name. ytitle Label y-axis, typically describing quantity measured (e.g., 'Number Patients', 'Frequency', 'Cost ($)'). Leave empty use default based weight variable. originaltheme Whether apply ggStatsPlot styling instead jamovi's default theme. ggStatsPlot theme provides statistical-publication ready formatting. Default jamovi theme integrates better jamovi analyses.

Clinical Applications: Disease Classification: Show distribution tumor grades, cancer stages, pathological subtypes Treatment Outcomes: Display response rates (complete/partial/response) across patient cohorts Demographic Analysis: Present patient characteristics, risk factors, comorbidity patterns Quality Metrics: Visualize compliance rates, diagnostic accuracy, safety outcomes Advantages Charts: intuitive pie charts showing proportions square = 1% makes percentages immediately clear Handles many categories better bar charts Effective presentations publications Faceting enables subgroup comparisons Statistical Considerations: effective n>=30; smaller samples may show unstable proportions Works best single category dominates (>80%) square represents approximately 1% sample Categories <5 cases may statistically unreliable Chi-square tests can evaluate proportion differences groups

title: Fagan Nomogram for Diagnostic Test Analysis — nomogrammer
text: Prevalence Prior probability (prevalence) number 0 1. represents probability disease test performed. Sens Model sensitivity number 0 1. probability test positive disease present. Optional Plr/Nlr provided. Spec Model specificity number 0 1. probability test negative disease absent. Optional Plr/Nlr provided. Plr Positive likelihood ratio (calculated Sens Spec provided). Must >= 1. provided along Nlr, takes precedence Sens/Spec. Nlr Negative likelihood ratio (calculated Sens Spec provided). Must 0 1. provided along Plr, takes precedence Sens/Spec. Detail Logical. TRUE, overlays key statistics (prevalence, likelihood ratios, posterior probabilities) onto plot. NullLine Logical. TRUE, adds reference line prior probability LR = 1 illustrate uninformative test. LabelSize Numeric. Controls size text labels plot. Default 14/5 ~= 2.8. Verbose Logical. TRUE, prints diagnostic metrics console.

title: Fagan Nomogram for Diagnostic Test Analysis — nomogrammer

title: Fagan Nomogram for Diagnostic Test Analysis — nomogrammer
text: Fagan nomogram visually represents Bayes' theorem diagnostic testing: $$Post-test odds = Pre-test odds x Likelihood ratio$$ function accepts either: Sensitivity Specificity (traditional approach) Positive Negative Likelihood Ratios (direct approach) provided, sensitivity/specificity take precedence warning issued. Mathematical relationships: PLR = Sensitivity / (1 - Specificity) NLR = (1 - Sensitivity) / Specificity calculating LRs: Specificity = (PLR - 1) / (PLR - NLR) calculating LRs: Sensitivity = PLR x (1 - Specificity) Post-test probability (+) = (Prevalence x PLR) / ((Prevalence x PLR) + (1 - Prevalence)) Post-test probability (-) = (Prevalence x NLR) / ((Prevalence x NLR) + (1 - Prevalence))

Unlike binary ROC dichotomizes outcomes, ordinal ROC preserves natural ordering categories accounts severity/progression inherent ordinal scales. analysis uses cumulative probability models proportional odds assumptions generate ROC curves reflect ordinal nature outcome. Provides cumulative AUC across thresholds, partial proportional odds models, ordinal-specific performance metrics. Essential biomarker validation grading systems, staging algorithms, scenario outcome 2 ordered levels. title: Outlier Detection — outlierdetection
text: data data data frame. vars Continuous variables analyze outliers. module detect outliers based selected variables using chosen detection methods. method_category Category outlier detection methods use. CLINICAL GUIDANCE: Univariate methods analyze variable separately (ideal lab values, vital signs). Multivariate methods consider relationships variables (useful correlated biomarkers). Composite combines multiple approaches robust detection (recommended clinical data). Examples: Use univariate hemoglobin levels, multivariate complete blood count panels. univariate_methods Specific univariate method outlier detection univariate category selected. multivariate_methods Specific multivariate method outlier detection multivariate category selected. composite_threshold Threshold composite outlier score (0.1-1.0). Default 0.5 means observations  classified outliers least half methods considered outliers. zscore_threshold Threshold Z-score based methods. CLINICAL EXAMPLES: 3.0 = 99.7 percent confidence (standard screening lab values), 3.29 = 99.9 percent confidence (stringent, critical values like cardiac enzymes), 2.5 = 98.8 percent confidence (sensitive detection research). Recommended: 3.29 clinical quality control. iqr_multiplier Multiplier IQR-based outlier detection. CLINICAL EXAMPLES: 1.5 = Tukey's standard (sensitive, may flag ~0.7 percent normal data), 1.7 = conservative (recommended clinical screening), 2.0 = conservative (critical biomarkers). Useful non-normal distributions common clinical data. confidence_level Confidence level interval-based methods (ETI, HDI). Default 99.9 percent identifies extreme observations. show_outlier_table Display comprehensive table outlier detection results including outlier scores, distances, classification observation. show_method_comparison Compare results across different detection methods using composite approach. show_exclusion_summary Provide summary observations recommended exclusion impact analysis. show_visualization Generate plots showing outlier detection results distribution outlier scores. show_interpretation Display detailed interpretation outlier detection results methodological notes.

text: data data data frame. vars Continuous variables include Principal Component Analysis. Select least 3 numeric variables. ncomp Number principal components test significance (1 20). Testing performed PC1 specified number components. nperm Number permutations generate null distribution (100-10000). Higher values provide accurate p-values take longer. Minimum p-value = 1/(nperm+1). p<0.001, use nperm>=1000. stop_rule Stop testing first non-significant component (Sequential Testing). Recommended: TRUE prevent Type error inflation. FALSE, components ncomp tested (Batch Testing). seed Random seed reproducibility permutation results. center Center variables mean = 0 PCA. Recommended: TRUE analyses. scale Scale variables standard deviation = 1 PCA. Recommended: TRUE variables different units scales. conflevel Confidence level confidence intervals (0.80-0.99). Default: 0.95 95 percent CI. adjustmethod Method adjusting p-values multiple testing. BH (Benjamini-Hochberg) controls false discovery rate. showpercent Display variance accounted (VAF) percentage (0-100) instead proportion (0-1). colororiginal Color original VAF line/points. Use color names hex codes. Default color-blind safe blue. colorpermuted Color permuted VAF line/points. Use color names hex codes. Default color-blind safe orange. showScreePlot Display scree plot eigenvalues. showLoadingsPlot Display plot variable loadings significant components. nLoadings Number top variables display loadings plot. plotwidth Width plot pixels. plotheight Height plot pixels. showSummary Display natural-language summary results clinical interpretation. title: Precision-Recall Analysis — prauc
text: Precision-Recall (PR) analysis superior ROC analysis highly imbalanced datasets, common digital pathology AI applications. ROC curves can misleading negative class vastly outnumbers positive class, PR curves focus performance minority (positive) class. area PR curve (PR-AUC Average Precision) provides single-number summary model performance. PR analysis essential evaluating rare event detection (mitotic figures <1 percent, rare tumor cells, micrometastases), cancer screening positives rare, quality control digital pathology defects uncommon, AI triage systems abnormal cases infrequent. module provides comprehensive PR analysis optimal threshold selection, comparison baseline (random classifier), F-score optimization different precision-recall trade-offs.

title: Precision-Recall Analysis — prauc
code: prauc(   data,   outcome,   predictor,   positive_level = "",   prevalence = -1,   calculate_auc = TRUE,   calculate_fscore = TRUE,   beta_weights = "1, 2, 0.5",   confidence_intervals = TRUE,   ci_method = "bootstrap",   bootstrap_samples = 1000,   confidence_level = 0.95,   compare_to_roc = TRUE,   baseline_comparison = TRUE,   interpolation_method = "step",   plot_pr_curve = TRUE,   plot_comparison = FALSE,   plot_fscore = FALSE,   min_threshold = 0,   max_threshold = 1,   random_seed = 12345 )

title: Precision-Recall Analysis — prauc
text: data data data frame. outcome Binary outcome variable (e.g., cancer/non-cancer, positive/negative). Must exactly two levels. predictor Continuous predictor variable (e.g., AI score, biomarker level, probability). Higher values indicate higher likelihood positive outcome. positive_level Level outcome variable treat "positive" class. specified, second level factor used. Critical correct PR analysis. prevalence Observed prevalence positive class dataset. Automatically calculated specified (-1). Used baseline comparison interpretation. calculate_auc Calculate area precision-recall curve (also called Average Precision). Uses trapezoidal integration. Essential summary metric imbalanced data. calculate_fscore Find optimal threshold maximizes F1-score (harmonic mean precision recall). Also calculates F2-score (emphasizes recall) F0.5-score (emphasizes precision). beta_weights Comma-separated list beta values F-score calculation. F1 (beta=1) balances precision recall. F2 (beta=2) weights recall higher. F0.5 (beta=0.5) weights precision higher. Example: "1, 2, 0.5, 3" confidence_intervals Calculate confidence intervals PR-AUC using bootstrap resampling. Provides uncertainty quantification imbalanced datasets. ci_method Method confidence interval calculation. Bootstrap percentile standard. BCa (bias-corrected accelerated) adjusts skewness. bootstrap_samples Number bootstrap resamples confidence interval calculation. confidence_level Confidence level interval estimation. compare_to_roc Calculate ROC-AUC comparison. Demonstrates advantage PR analysis imbalanced data ROC-AUC may misleadingly high. baseline_comparison Compare PR-AUC baseline (random classifier). Baseline PR-AUC equals prevalence. Shows improvement chance performance. interpolation_method Method interpolating PR curve points. Step function standard PR curves. Linear interpolation can smooth curve. plot_pr_curve Plot precision-recall curve optimal F-score threshold marked. Shows trade-precision recall across thresholds. plot_comparison Side--side comparison ROC PR curves demonstrate differences imbalanced dataset evaluation. plot_fscore Plot F-scores (F1, F2, F0.5) across thresholds visualize optimal operating points different precision-recall trade-offs. min_threshold Minimum predictor threshold evaluate. Use focus clinically relevant range. max_threshold Maximum predictor threshold evaluate. random_seed Random seed bootstrap procedures ensure reproducibility.
