title: Advanced ROC Analysis — psychopdaROC
text: manualRun TRUE, results computed clicking Run button. Useful skipping intermediate recomputes adjusting options slow bootstrap cutpoint analyses. run . clinicalMode Select complexity level analysis: Basic - Essential ROC metrics clinical decision making Advanced - Additional statistical comparisons metrics Comprehensive - Full research-grade analysis options data data data frame. dependentVars Test variable(s) evaluated classification performance. Multiple variables can selected comparison. classVar Binary classification variable representing true class (gold standard). Must exactly two levels. positiveClass Specifies level class variable treated positive class. subGroup Optional grouping variable stratified analysis. ROC curves calculated separately group. clinicalPreset Choose preset configuration optimized specific clinical scenarios: Screening - High sensitivity avoid missing cases Confirmation - High specificity avoid false positives Balanced - Equal weight sensitivity specificity Research - Comprehensive analysis publication method Method determining optimal cutpoint. Different methods optimize different aspects classifier performance. metric Metric optimize determining cutpoint.  applies maximize/minimize methods. direction Direction classification relative cutpoint. Use '>=' higher test values indicate positive class. specifyCutScore Specific cutpoint value use method set 'Manual cutpoint'. tol_metric Tolerance metric value multiple cutpoints yield similar performance. Cutpoints within tolerance considered equivalent. break_ties Method handling ties multiple cutpoints achieve metric value. allObserved Display performance metrics observed test values potential cutpoints, just optimal cutpoint. boot_runs Number bootstrap iterations methods using bootstrapping. Set 0 disable bootstrapping. seed Random seed reproducibility bootstrap permutation tests. usePriorPrev Use specified prior prevalence instead sample prevalence calculating predictive values. priorPrev Population prevalence use predictive value calculations. used 'Use Prior Prevalence' checked. costratioFP Relative cost false positives compared false negatives. Values > 1 penalize false positives heavily. sensSpecTable Display detailed confusion matrices optimal cutpoints. showThresholdTable Display detailed table performance metrics multiple thresholds. maxThresholds Maximum number threshold values show threshold table. delongTest Test whether diagnostic performance differs significantly multiple tests. Uses DeLong's method compare Area Curve (AUC) values. Requires least two test variables. plotROC Display ROC curves visual assessment classifier performance. combinePlots multiple test variables selected, combine ROC curves single plot. cleanPlot Create clean ROC curves without annotations, suitable publications. showOptimalPoint Display optimal cutpoint ROC curve. displaySE Display standard error bands ROC curves (LOESS smoothing applied). smoothing Apply LOESS smoothing ROC curves visualization. showConfidenceBands Display confidence bands around ROC curve. legendPosition Position legend plots multiple ROC curves. directLabel Label curves directly plot instead using legend. interactiveROC Create interactive HTML ROC plot (requires plotROC package). showCriterionPlot Plot showing sensitivity specificity change across different thresholds. showPrevalencePlot Plot showing PPV NPV change disease prevalence. showDotPlot Dot plot showing distribution test values class. precisionRecallCurve Display precision-recall curves alongside ROC curves. partialAUC Calculate AUC specific region ROC curve. partialAUCfrom Lower bound specificity range partial AUC calculation. partialAUCto Upper bound specificity range partial AUC calculation. rocSmoothingMethod Method smoothing ROC curve (requires pROC package). bootstrapCI Calculate bootstrap confidence intervals AUC optimal cutpoints. bootstrapReps Number bootstrap replications confidence interval calculation. quantileCIs Display confidence intervals specific quantiles test variable. quantiles Comma-separated list quantiles (0-1) display confidence intervals. compareClassifiers Perform comprehensive comparison classifier performance metrics. calculateIDI Calculate much better one test discriminating diseased healthy patients. IDI (Integrated Discrimination Improvement) measures average improvement predicted probabilities. calculateNRI Calculate many patients correctly reclassified using new test. NRI (Net Reclassification Index) measures net improvement patient classification. refVar Reference test variable IDI NRI calculations. variables compared reference. nriThresholds Comma-separated probability thresholds (0-1) defining risk categories NRI. Leave empty continuous NRI. idiNriBootRuns Number bootstrap iterations IDI NRI confidence intervals. effectSizeAnalysis Calculate effect sizes ROC curve differences using Cohen's conventions standardized mean differences AUC values. powerAnalysis Perform statistical power analysis ROC curve comparisons including sample size estimation power calculations detecting AUC differences. powerAnalysisType Type power analysis perform. expectedAUCDifference Expected difference AUC values power calculations sample size estimation. targetPower Target statistical power sample size calculations (typically 0.8 0.9). significanceLevel Type error rate power calculations (typically 0.05). correlationROCs Expected correlation paired ROC curves power calculations. Use 0.5 moderate correlation, 0.0 independent samples. bayesianAnalysis Perform bootstrap-based ROC analysis optional prior weighting estimate uncertainty AUC. Uses bootstrap resampling create empirical distribution. NOTE: full Bayesian MCMC inference; uses bootstrap simulation prior parameters weights. Interpret "credible intervals" bootstrap percentile confidence intervals. priorAUC Prior belief AUC value Bayesian analysis (center prior distribution). priorPrecision Precision prior belief (higher values = confident prior). clinicalUtilityAnalysis Perform clinical utility analysis including net benefit curves, decision curve analysis, clinical impact assessment. treatmentThreshold Treatment threshold range decision curve analysis (min,max,step). Example: "0.05,0.5,0.05" creates thresholds 5 percent 50 percent 5 percent steps. harmBenefitRatio Ratio harm unnecessary treatment benefit necessary treatment. Lower values favor aggressive treatment policies. interventionCost Include cost-effectiveness considerations clinical utility analysis. fixedSensSpecAnalysis Determine cutoffs based fixed sensitivity specificity values display corresponding performance metrics. fixedAnalysisType Choose whether fix sensitivity specificity value cutoff determination. fixedSensitivityValue Target sensitivity value (0-1) determining corresponding cutoff specificity. fixedSpecificityValue Target specificity value (0-1) determining corresponding cutoff sensitivity. showFixedROC Display separate ROC curve highlighting fixed sensitivity/specificity point. fixedInterpolation Method interpolating observed points achieve target sensitivity/specificity. showFixedExplanation Display explanatory guide fixed sensitivity/specificity analysis including  clinical interpretation, interpolation methods, usage recommendations. metaAnalysis Perform meta-analysis AUC values across multiple test variables. Requires least 3 test variables enable pooled effect estimation. metaAnalysisMethod Statistical method combining AUC estimates across studies/variables. heterogeneityTest Perform Cochran's Q test calculate ² statistic assess heterogeneity AUC estimates. forestPlot Create forest plot visualization individual pooled AUC estimates confidence intervals. overrideMetaAnalysisWarning ADVANCED OPTION: Bypass independence assumption check meta-analysis. WARNING - use fully understand statistical implications. Meta-analysis non-independent data produces invalid results used formal inference. Use DeLong's test instead within-study comparisons multiple markers.

title: Q-TWiST Analysis — qtwist
text: data Dataset containing overall survival, progression-free survival, toxicity information. time_os Time death censoring consistent units (months recommended). represents total follow-time randomization/enrollment. event_os Event indicator overall survival. Can numeric (1=death, 0=censored) factor (specify death level ). event_os_level level indicating death using factor variables (e.g., "Dead", "Deceased"). numeric, use level "1" death. time_pfs Time disease progression, relapse, death (whichever comes first). Must units overall survival time. PFS time <= OS time patient. event_pfs Event indicator progression-free survival. 1 = progression death, 0 = censored (specify factor level). event_pfs_level level indicating progression death using factor variables. treatment Treatment group variable comparison. Q-TWiST analysis requires exactly 2 treatment groups comparison. analysis use available levels (must exactly 2 groups). toxicity_method Method defining toxicity (TOX) period Q-TWiST analysis. Fixed window uses period patients; individual duration allows patient-specific toxicity times. toxicity_window Duration toxicity assessment window months (default: 3 months). Commonly used values: 3 months (1 treatment cycle), 6 months (adjuvant therapy). defines TOX period patients using fixed window method. toxicity_probability Proportion patients experiencing grade 3-4 toxicity window. Used toxicity indicator variable provided. Can estimated pilot data literature. toxicity_duration_var Variable containing individual patient toxicity durations (months). patients without toxicity, use 0. toxicity, specify duration grade 3-4 adverse events. toxicity_indicator_var Optional binary indicator whether patient experienced grade 3-4 toxicity. provided, used weight toxicity time calculations. toxicity_indicator_level Level indicating presence grade 3-4 toxicity (e.g., "Yes", "Grade 3-4", 1). toxicity_start_var Time toxicity begins (months baseline). Use 0 toxicity starting treatment initiation. toxicity_end_var Time toxicity resolves (months baseline). TOX duration = toxicity_end - toxicity_start. tau Restricted time horizon Q-TWiST analysis months. survival estimates restricted maximum follow-time. Common values: 24 months (2 years), 36 months (3 years), 60 months (5 years). Choose based median survival clinical relevance. tau_selection Method selecting time horizon (tau). User-specified allows manual entry; automatic methods select based data characteristics. utility_tox Quality--life utility weight time treatment toxicity. 0 = worst possible health, 1 = perfect health. Typical range: 0.3-0.7 depending toxicity severity. Literature values: chemotherapy toxicity ≈ 0.5, severe toxicity ≈ 0.3. utility_twist Quality--life utility weight time without symptoms toxicity. Typically set 1.0 (perfect health) reference state. generally >= utility_tox >= utility_rel. utility_rel Quality--life utility weight time disease relapse/progression. Accounts symptomatic disease burden. Typical range: 0.3-0.6 depending disease severity symptoms. Literature values: metastatic disease ≈ 0.5, symptomatic relapse ≈ 0.4. sensitivity_analysis Examine Q-TWiST results vary across different utility weight assumptions. Essential robust conclusions, utility weights subjective. Shows treatment preference changes based quality--life values. utility_range_tox Comma-separated list utility values TOX state sensitivity analysis. Example: "0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0" utility_range_rel Comma-separated list utility values REL state sensitivity analysis. threshold_analysis Find threshold utility values treatment preference changes. Identifies "break-even" points clinical decision-making. confidence_level Confidence level interval estimation (default: 0.95 95 percent CI). bootstrap_ci Use bootstrap resampling calculate confidence intervals Q-TWiST treatment differences. Recommended robust inference. bootstrap_samples Number bootstrap resamples confidence interval calculation. samples = precise estimates longer computation time. 1000 samples usually sufficient; use 2000+ publication. bootstrap_seed Random seed bootstrap sampling (reproducibility). stratify_by Variables stratified analysis (e.g., site, stage, biomarker status). Separate Q-TWiST analyses performed stratum. pooled_analysis Display overall Q-TWiST results addition stratified results. show_state_partition Display table showing mean time spent health state (TOX, TWiST, REL) treatment arm. show_qtwist_scores Display quality-adjusted survival (Q-TWiST) scores treatment applied utility weights. show_treatment_difference Display Q-TWiST difference treatment arms confidence intervals statistical significance. show_sensitivity_table Display results across varying utility weight combinations. show_rmst_components Show underlying restricted mean survival time calculations overall survival progression-free survival. show_descriptive_stats Display sample sizes, median survival times, event rates treatment arm. plot_partitioned_survival Display stacked area plot showing TOX, TWiST, REL components time treatment arm. plot_qtwist_comparison Bar chart comparing Q-TWiST components (TOX, TWiST, REL) treatment arms utility weights applied. plot_sensitivity Contour plot heatmap showing Q-TWiST treatment difference across varying utility weight combinations. plot_km_curves Display standard Kaplan-Meier survival curves OS PFS reference alongside Q-TWiST results. plot_color_scheme Color scheme partitioned survival plots. TOX (toxicity), TWiST (good quality), REL (relapse) states. showExplanations Include detailed explanations Q-TWiST methodology, interpretation guidance, clinical significance. showClinicalGuidance Provide clinical interpretation assistance including treatment implications decision-making considerations. showFormulas Display mathematical formulas Q-TWiST calculations statistical tests. showReferences Display key references Q-TWiST methodology applications.

title: Q-TWiST Analysis — qtwist
text: Q-TWiST : Partitions overall survival three health states different quality--life weights: TOX: Time treatment toxicity (typically μ = 0-0.5) TWiST: Time without symptoms toxicity (μ = 1.0, perfect health) REL: Time disease relapse/progression (typically μ = 0-0.5) Key Features: State-based survival partitioning clinical significance Utility weight application quality adjustment Sensitivity analysis across utility values Bootstrap confidence intervals treatment differences Visual comparison partitioned survival plots Clinical Applications: Adjuvant therapy evaluation (balancing toxicity vs. benefit) Treatment comparison survival similar quality differs Shared decision-making (patient-relevant quality metrics) Regulatory submissions (FDA/EMA recognized endpoint)

text: Creates Raincloud plots visualize data distributions using ggdist package. Raincloud plots combine three visualization techniques: half-violin plots showing distribution density, box plots showing summary statistics, dot plots showing individual data points. provides comprehensive view data distribution reveals patterns traditional box plots might miss, including multimodality distribution shape. title: ROC Regression (Covariate-Adjusted ROC) — rocreg
text: ROC regression covariate-adjusted diagnostic accuracy assessment. Traditional ROC analysis assumes diagnostic test performance constant across patients, accuracy often varies patient characteristics (age, disease stage, scanner type, staining protocol). ROC regression models sensitivity specificity change functions covariates, providing covariate-specific ROC curves adjusted summary measures (covariate-adjusted AUC). Essential comparing diagnostic tests across heterogeneous populations, adjusting confounders test comparison studies, identifying patient subgroups tests perform differently. Particularly valuable digital pathology accounting batch effects (different scanners, institutions, staining protocols) biomarker studies age/stage-specific performance assessment. Uses binormal, non-parametric, Bayesian approaches model covariate effects ROC curves. Provides population-averaged covariate-specific diagnostic accuracy estimates.

Examples: age, sex, disease stage, scanner type, institution, staining batch. continuous categorical covariates supported. covariate_effects model covariate effects. "" allows different effects diseased non-diseased groups, "sensitivity" models effects diseased, "specificity" non-diseased. method Method ROC regression. title: Simon-Makuch Time-Dependent Survival Analysis — simonmakuch
text: Performs comprehensive survival analysis time-dependent variables using Simon-Makuch method. specialized analysis addresses critical challenge immortal time bias studying treatments, biomarkers, exposures change patient follow-. Clinical Applications: - Treatment effectiveness therapy timing varies (e.g., adjuvant therapy, targeted agents) - Biomarker evolution studies (e.g., mutation status, protein expression changes) - Disease progression impact outcomes (e.g., metastasis development, grade progression) - Healthcare intervention timing effects (e.g., surgery, radiation, supportive care) Key Statistical Methods: - Simon-Makuch plots: Modified Kaplan-Meier curves time-dependent exposures - Landmark analysis: Conditional survival fixed time points - Time-dependent Cox regression: Hazard ratios accounting exposure timing - Immortal time bias assessment: Comparison naive vs. proper methods - Mantel-Byar testing: Specialized tests time-dependent comparisons Use Simon-Makuch Analysis: Standard survival analysis assumes fixed baseline characteristics, leading immortal time bias exposures change follow-. Simon-Makuch methods properly account timing exposure changes, providing unbiased survival estimates valid statistical comparisons.

text: data . intersections Number grid intersections (hits) structure interest (e.g., vessels, nuclei, fibrosis areas). totalPoints Total number grid points test lines used measurement. boundaryIntersections Number grid line intersections object boundaries (boundary density calculation). objectCount Number discrete objects counted (numerical density calculation). referenceArea Total reference area examined (square micrometers). Typically calculated : image width × height. sectionThickness Histological section thickness micrometers. Required volume density calculations. Default: 5 μm. gridSpacing Distance grid lines micrometers. title: Example Vessel Density Data for Stereology Analysis — stereology_vessel_data
text: Simulated data based stereology principles : Kayser et al. (2009) Diagnostic Pathology 4:6. Realistic vessel density values based published tumor angiogenesis studies.

title: Example Vessel Density Data for Stereology Analysis — stereology_vessel_data
text: Study Design: 50 histological images 3 diagnostic groups Systematic 10x10 grid overlay (100 points per image) Grid spacing: 10 um Reference area: 1000x1000 um (1 mm^2) Section thickness: 5 um (standard histology) Clinical Context: Vessel density critical parameter tumor pathology. Malignant tumors often show increased angiogenesis (new blood vessel formation) support rapid growth. Stereology provides unbiased quantification vessel density 2D histological sections without requiring 3D reconstruction. Vessel Density Diagnosis: Normal tissue: Low vessel density (Aa ~ 0.05-0.10) Benign tumors: Moderate vessel density (Aa ~ 0.15-0.25) Malignant tumors: High vessel density (Aa ~ 0.30-0.50) due angiogenesis Stereological Parameters: Area Density (Aa) Formula: Aa = intersections / total_points Meaning: Fraction tissue area occupied vessels Use: Primary measure vessel density Volume Density (Vv) Formula: Vv = Aa (isotropic random sections) Meaning: Fraction tissue volume occupied vessels Use: 3D estimate 2D sections Boundary Density (Ba) Formula: Ba = (2 x boundary_intersections) / line_length Meaning: Vessel boundary length per unit area Use: Measure vessel complexity Numerical Density (Na) Formula: Na = object_count / reference_area Meaning: Number vessels per unit area Use: Vessel count density Surface Density (Sv) Formula: Sv = 2 x Ba Meaning: Vessel surface area per unit volume Use: Exchange surface quantification Example Analysis: Stereology Needed: Provides unbiased estimates 3D parameters 2D sections need complex 3D reconstruction Well-established statistical properties Reproducible across laboratories Applicable histological structure Expected Results: Malignant tumors show significantly higher vessel density (Aa ~ 0.39) Benign tumors intermediate density (Aa ~ 0.20) Normal tissue lowest density (Aa ~ 0.07) Statistical tests show significant differences groups Quality Control: Grid spacing appropriate vessel size (10 um) Adequate number points per image (100 points) Multiple images per diagnosis (16-17 per group) Systematic random sampling approach

text: data data data frame. outcome Primary outcome variable. survival analysis, time variable. binary outcomes, use 0/1 factor 2 levels. continuous outcomes, use numeric variables. treatment Treatment exposure variable (must binary: 0/1, control/treatment). variable defines two groups compared analysis. subgroups Variables defining patient subgroups analysis (categorical variables). variable analyzed separately identify differential treatment effects. Required survival analysis distinguish observed events censored observations. outcomeType Type outcome variable: "survival" (time--event), "binary" (yes/), "continuous". Determines statistical method used analysis (Cox regression, logistic regression, linear regression). effectMeasure Statistical measure treatment effect: "hr" (hazard ratio), "" (odds ratio),  "rr" (risk ratio), "md" (mean difference). match outcome type. confidenceLevel Confidence level intervals. showOverall Display overall treatment effect across patients. showInteraction Perform statistical tests subgroup interactions using likelihood ratio tests. title: Survival Feature Ranking — survivalfeaturerank
text: data dataset analyzed, provided data frame. survtime numeric variable representing follow-time event censoring. event event indicator variable (e.g., death, recurrence). coded 1 = event, 0 = censored, factor one level represents event. eventLevel level event variable represents event interest. numeric variables, typically "1". factors, select appropriate level. features Variables tested individually association survival. variable tested separate univariate Cox model. Can include categorical continuous variables. rankBy Criterion ranking features: - pvalue: Sorts statistical significance (smallest p-value first) - hazard: Sorts effect size (hazard ratio furthest 1) - cindex: Sorts discriminative ability (highest C-index first) showCI true, displays 95 percent confidence intervals hazard ratios results table. adjustPValues true, applies multiple testing correction p-values. Recommended testing many features control false discovery rate. adjustMethod Method p-value adjustment. FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg) recommended exploratory analysis. Bonferroni conservative. showForestPlot true, generates forest plot showing hazard ratios confidence intervals features, sorted ranking criterion. forestStyle Visual style forest plot. showTopKM true, generates Kaplan-Meier survival curves top-ranked features. Useful visualizing survival differences important predictors. topN Number top-ranked features generate Kaplan-Meier plots. used "Show Kaplan-Meier Plots Top Features" enabled. kmLayout Layout multiple Kaplan-Meier plots. Separate shows one plot per feature, faceted shows grid. endplot Maximum follow-time display Kaplan-Meier plots. byplot Interval time axis labels plots. risktable true, displays number risk Kaplan-Meier plots. pplot true, displays log-rank test p-values Kaplan-Meier plots. showSummary true, displays summary statistics including total number features tested, number significant features, interpretation guidance. alphaLevel Significance level highlighting significant features results table. showFullTable true, shows results tested features. false, shows statistically significant features.

text: data data data frame containing date columns interval calculation. dx_date Column containing start dates (e.g., diagnosis date, study entry, treatment start). Supports various date formats including text numeric representations. fu_date Column containing end dates (e.g., follow-date, event date, study exit). Must format start date variable. time_format Date format specification. 'Auto-detect' attempts identify format automatically. Manual selection ensures accurate parsing specific date formats. output_unit Unit calculated time intervals. Affects person-time calculations  statistical summaries. Choose based study duration event frequency. time_basis Controls months/years computed. Standardized uses fixed lengths (30.44 days per month, 365.25 days per year) suited person-time denominators. Calendar-aware respects actual month lengths (28 31 days) converting intervals months/years. use_landmark Enables conditional analysis specific time point. Useful  studying outcomes landmark time (e.g., 6-month survivors ). landmark_time Time point landmark analysis specified output units.  participants surviving past time included analysis. remove_negative Automatically exclude negative time intervals (end date start date). Recommended data quality assurance. remove_extreme Identify flag potentially extreme time intervals quality review. Uses statistical outlier detection methods. extreme_multiplier Multiplier 99th percentile define extreme values. Default 2.0 means values >2× 99th percentile flagged. Higher values conservative (fewer flagged values). add_times Appends calculated time intervals new variable downstream analysis. Useful subsequent survival analysis person-time calculations. include_quality_metrics Provides comprehensive data quality assessment including missing values, negative intervals, distribution statistics. confidence_level Confidence level statistical intervals (mean confidence intervals). Standard epidemiological practice uses 95 percent confidence intervals. show_summary Generate plain-language interpretation results suitable copying reports clinical notes. show_glossary Display definitions key terms (person-time, incidence rate, landmark analysis, etc.) help interpret results. timezone Timezone datetime parsing. 'System Default' uses computer's timezone. 'UTC' interprets datetimes Coordinated Universal Time. Ensures consistent time interval calculations across different systems time zones.

title: Trichotomous (Three-way) ROC Analysis — trichotomousroc
text: Trichotomous ROC analysis three-category diagnostic tests positive, indeterminate (grey zone), negative outcomes. Essential biomarker scoring systems like HER2 (0-1+/2+/3+), PD-L1 expression levels, cytology classifications "atypical" results. Unlike binary ROC considers positive vs negative, trichotomous ROC accounts clinically important indeterminate zone additional testing may required. analysis provides 3×3 confusion matrices, category-specific sensitivities specificities, volume ROC surface (VUS) 3D extension AUC, optimal threshold determination decision boundary. Particularly valuable establishing clinical cutoffs molecular pathology grey-zone results trigger reflex testing (e.g., HER2 2+ requires FISH confirmation).

title: Trichotomous (Three-way) ROC Analysis — trichotomousroc

title: Trichotomous (Three-way) ROC Analysis — trichotomousroc
text: data data data frame. predictor Continuous predictor variable (e.g., IHC H-score, gene expression level, AI probability score) used classify cases three categories. outcome Three-level gold standard outcome variable defining true classification (positive/indeterminate/negative diseased/borderline/healthy). positive_level Level outcome variable representing definite positive/diseased cases. indeterminate_level Level outcome variable representing indeterminate/borderline/grey zone cases. negative_level Level outcome variable representing definite negative/non-diseased cases. threshold_method Method determining two thresholds separate three categories. Youden maximizes overall correct classification, clinical uses cost-benefit analysis, fixed allows manual threshold specification, tertile divides equal thirds. lower_threshold Lower threshold value using fixed threshold method. Values classified negative. Required threshold_method = 'fixed'. upper_threshold Upper threshold value using fixed threshold method. Values classified positive. Required threshold_method = 'fixed'. cost_fn Relative cost misclassifying positive case negative. Higher values increase sensitivity expense specificity. cost_fp Relative cost misclassifying negative case positive. Higher values increase specificity expense sensitivity. cost_indeterminate Relative cost classifying case indeterminate (requiring additional testing). Typically lower definite misclassification higher correct classification. confidence_level Confidence level intervals around VUS performance metrics. bootstrap_samples Number bootstrap samples confidence interval estimation. samples provide stable estimates increase computation time. bootstrap_method Bootstrap confidence interval method. BCa provides bias-corrected intervals. calculate_vus Calculate Volume ROC Surface, 3D extension AUC three categories. VUS ranges 0 1, 0.167 represents random classification 1 represents perfect classification. Values > 0.167 indicate discriminatory ability. category_sensitivities Calculate sensitivity category (ability correctly identify positive, indeterminate, negative cases respectively). pairwise_comparisons Perform binary ROC analysis three pairwise comparisons: positive vs negative (ignoring indeterminate), positive vs indeterminate, indeterminate vs negative. confusion_matrix_3x3 Display full 3×3 confusion matrix showing possible classification outcomes. Rows represent true categories, columns represent predicted categories. plot_3d_surface Create 3D visualization ROC surface. surface extends 2D ROC curve three dimensions, showing classification performance across threshold combinations. plot_threshold_analysis Plot showing classification metrics vary different threshold combinations. Helps visualize trade-definite indeterminate classifications. plot_category_distributions Display distribution predictor scores outcome category threshold lines showing decision boundaries. plot_pairwise_rocs Show three pairwise binary ROC curves comparison trichotomous analysis. clinical_context Clinical context interpretation assistance. Provides context-specific guidance threshold selection clinical implications. show_clinical_interpretation Provide clinical interpretation results including recommendations threshold use implications patient management. indeterminate_action Specify clinical action cases classified indeterminate. affects interpretation diagnostic performance metrics. stratified_analysis Perform stratified trichotomous ROC analysis important subgroups assess consistency across populations. stratify_by Variable defining strata stratified analysis. level receive separate trichotomous ROC analysis. missing_handling Method handling missing data predictor outcome variables. random_seed Random seed bootstrap sampling. Ensures reproducible results.

title: Volume Under ROC Surface (VUS) Analysis — vusanalysis
text: Volume ROC Surface (VUS) analysis extends traditional Area ROC Curve (AUC) diagnostic tests three ordered classes. binary ROC analysis calculates area 2D curve, VUS calculates volume 3D surface multi-class problems. VUS represents probability randomly selected triple observations (one class) correctly ordered diagnostic marker. VUS ranges 0 1, 0.5 indicates random classification (discrimination), 1 indicates perfect discrimination across classes. method particularly valuable tumor grading (Grade 1/2/3), disease staging (Stage /II/III/IV), severity classification (mild/moderate/severe), diagnostic scenario outcomes naturally fall three ordered categories. analysis provides pairwise AUC comparisons adjacent classes, overall VUS confidence intervals, hypothesis testing chance performance. Essential validating biomarkers, imaging features, AI models multi-class clinicopathological applications binary classification insufficient.

text: data data data frame LESION-LEVEL observations (one row per lesion per timepoint). patientID Variable containing patient identifiers. patient can multiple lesions tracked across timepoints. lesionID Unique lesion identifier within patient (e.g., L1, L2, Liver_1, Lung_2). Used track individual lesions across timepoints. visitTime Time point measurement (e.g., weeks baseline, days treatment start). Baseline time = 0. Used tracking lesion progression time. lesionType Lesion classification: Target, NonTarget, New. Target lesions (max 5 total, max 2 per organ) measured summed. NonTarget lesions assessed qualitatively (present/absent/progressed). location Anatomic site lesion (e.g., Liver, Lung, Lymph_Node). Used enforce RECIST rule: max 2 target lesions per organ. diameter Longest diameter target lesions millimeters (>=10mm non-lymph nodes, >=15mm lymph nodes). non-target lesions, can NA (qualitative assessment ). isNewLesion Binary indicator (0 = baseline/existing, 1 = new lesion appearing baseline). new lesion automatically triggers Progressive Disease (PD) per RECIST v1.1. baselineTimepoint Value visitTime representing baseline (default = 0). lesions timepoint establish baseline sum. confirmationInterval Minimum time interval (weeks) response confirmation per RECIST v1.1. title: ClinicoPath 0.0.34

text: Package Dependencies: R6, jmvcore, survival, survminer, ggplot2, dplyr Key Algorithms: Endpoint Validation:
code: # Time Calculation (Date Input) if (inputType == 'dates') {   # Calculate difference in days   diff_days <- as.numeric(difftime(end_date, start_date, units = "days"))    # Convert to selected unit   time <- switch(timeUnit,     days = diff_days,     weeks = diff_days / 7,     months = diff_days / 30.4375,  # Average month     years = diff_days / 365.25      # Account for leap years   ) }  # PFS Derivation pfs_event <- pmax(progression_event, death_event, na.rm = TRUE) # Event = 1 if EITHER progression OR death occurred  # Summary Statistics surv_obj <- Surv(time, event) km_fit <- survfit(surv_obj ~ 1) median_survival <- summary(km_fit)$table["median"] ci_95 <- summary(km_fit)$table[c("0.95LCL", "0.95UCL")]  # Milestone Analysis surv_summary <- summary(km_fit, times = c(6, 12, 24), extend = TRUE) # Returns survival probability, CI, and n at risk at each milestone # Data Quality Checks - Missing patient IDs flagged - Invalid dates detected (end before start) - Event indicator validation (0/1 only) - Response date required for DOR - Treatment end required for Time on Treatment  # Summary Tables Include - N patients with valid data per endpoint - Number of events vs censored - Event rates and censoring rates - Median survival with 95% CI - Milestone survival probabilities

title: ClinicoPath 0.0.32.11
text: Type: Non-breaking enhancement existing module New Feature: Multi-method CI comparison sample size planning Purpose: Compare sample size requirements across different confidence interval methods CI Methods Compared: Clopper-Pearson (Exact): Reference standard, exact binomial based beta distribution Wilson Score: Adjustment continuity, better coverage near extremes Agresti-Coull: Add z²/2 successes, improved normal approximation Normal Approximation (Wald): Simple poor coverage extreme p small n Comparison Output: N required sensitivity (diseased cases needed) N required specificity (non-diseased cases needed) Total N required (maximum sensitivity/specificity needs) Relative efficiency (%): Shows method’s efficiency vs Clopper-Pearson baseline Interpretation Guide: Efficiency >100%: Method requires fewer subjects (less conservative) Efficiency <100%: Method requires subjects (conservative) Clopper-Pearson (100%): conservative, guaranteed coverage Use Cases: Justifying choice CI method study protocols Sensitivity analysis sample size planning Understanding trade-offs exact approximate methods Budget-constrained studies comparing feasibility Toggle: Optional feature, disabled default (show_method_comparison checkbox)

title: ClinicoPath 0.0.32.10
text: Purpose: Quantify AI prediction uncertainty information gain Shannon Entropy Formula: H(X) = -Σ p(x) × log₂(p(x)) Range: 0 (perfect certainty) 1 (maximum uncertainty, normalized) Normalized log₂(n_classes) interpretability Mutual Information Formula: (X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) Measures much knowing X reduces uncertainty Y Normalized MI ∈ [0,1]: (X;Y) / min(H(X), H(Y)) Applications: AI Triage: Flag high-uncertainty predictions human review Feature Selection: Identify features high MI outcome Test Ordering: Prioritize tests maximizing information gain Multi-class Uncertainty: Quantify confidence AI classification Key Features: Case-level entropy calculation Entropy distribution true class High-uncertainty threshold flagging Conditional entropy H(Y|X) KL divergence uniform distribution Binning methods continuous variables (equal width, equal frequency, Sturges) High entropy + correct → Lucky guess, review case Low entropy + incorrect → Systematic error, investigate Uncertainty Interpretation (normalized entropy): 0.0-0.3: Low uncertainty (confident prediction) 0.3-0.7: Moderate uncertainty (consider human review) 0.7-1.0: High uncertainty (defer expert)
